# EAFIT's new master's program aims to train organizational psychologists to innovate in the world of work

**The Master's program in Work and Organizational Psychology—a professional development program lasting three semesters—is the University's newest postgraduate offering. Applications are now being accepted for the first cohort.**

**With the development of a clinical-critical and interdisciplinary vision of the problems of study that correspond to the field of work and organizations, this postgraduate program, attached to the School of Humanities, seeks to train masters in organizational psychology with an integral vision of companies and human talent.**

- [Start](https://www.eafit.edu.co/)
- [News](https://www.eafit.edu.co/noticias)
- [Our Impact](https://www.eafit.edu.co/noticias/nuestro-impacto)
- EAFIT's New Master's Program Aims to Train Organizational Psychologists to Innovate in the World of Work

![Image: EAFIT's new master's program aims to train organizational psychologists to innovate in the world of work](https://universidadeafit.widen.net/content/86bfa125-2ba0-4acd-9ec3-76022a0377a2/web/formar-psicologos.jpg?crop=yes&k=c&w=823&h=450&itok=CqNHX_TM)

The Master's program in Work and Organizational Psychology recognizes the relationship between the individual, work, and context as its object of study. It considers work as a human activity and develops within the specific setting of organizations.

From a clinical-critical and interdisciplinary perspective of business organizations to improve the performance of people in the world of work, the Master's in Work and Organizational Psychology of EAFIT is born, the new program at this training level that is incorporated into the academic offer of the University.

Currently, the postgraduate program has an open enrollment process through the Institution's website, where interested parties can learn about the professional profile, financing options, and receive guidance from academic agents of the program with a view to starting in 2021.

Lasting three semesters and with a professional focus, the master's program is aimed at professionals in fields such as psychology, administration, sociology, communication, and social sciences, among other related disciplines. "Many people have wanted specialized training in psychology within organizations. There are few programs of this kind in the country, even though postgraduate studies in this field have been promoted for some time," says Jonny Javier Orejuela Gómez, coordinator of the Master's Program in Work and Organizational Psychology.

"This program aims to address that need, especially since many psychologists may find their first job in areas related to human resource management and organizational development. This leads us to believe that these individuals currently working in organizations may require specialized training in this area," adds the expert in social psychology of work, who is part of the faculty of the new program.

This postgraduate program bears the EAFIT seal and is backed by its academic tradition in organizational management, the world of work, and business. According to the expert faculty, this training is expected to equip graduates to work as consultants or analysts for various organizations, fostering a better quality of life in the workplace—in other words, contributing to human well-being and facilitating optimal conditions for business productivity.

###### Human well-being in organizations

Based on the academic findings made by the Psychology Department of EAFIT, the Master's in Work and Organizational Psychology seeks to put into practice and transmit all the wealth of knowledge developed in recent years as part of the clinical field of work and organizations, an area little known in several Latin American countries but which is very widespread in places like Brazil, Canada and France.

This approach refers precisely to the clinical and critical perspective that allows for recognizing individuals in their uniqueness, based on the ability to listen to human needs in order to improve quality of life within the workplace. As a precursor to this master's program, the University has offered several diploma courses, especially for private companies and the general public.

"Work and organizational psychology has been reduced to practical processes such as selection, workshops, and training, but the true essence of its deeper study lies in considering the organization as a whole, taking into account the individual, groups, the organization itself, and the context. In this way, it becomes a strategic ally for senior management, because by reflecting on these issues, it fosters sensitivity and the ability to act as an intermediary between operational and managerial levels, seeking to provide effective solutions to different problems and needs through management and intervention," states Milena Margarita Villamizar Reyes, Master of Psychology with an emphasis on Organizational Psychology from the Department of Psychology at EAFIT University, and a professor in the Master's program.

This profile brings together interdisciplinary knowledge from clinical psychology, sociology, social work, law, and other fields. From its critical perspective, it seeks to challenge the discourse of capitalism in order to foster well-being within the organization of work. Therefore, one of the postgraduate program's objectives is to offer tools for intervening in organizations to improve human performance without neglecting the quality of life of workers. This program is supported by the research groups in Psychological Studies and Analytical Methods and their Applications in the Social Sciences and Humanities (EAFIT-University of Antioquia).

"We will have approaches to applying general psychology and clinical psychology in organizational contexts. The master's program includes the analysis of the behavior of individuals and the processes that give life to an organization," says Professor Milena Villamizar, an expert in human resource management and a researcher with the Psychology Studies group in the clinical, work, and society line.

Currently, the two main areas in which psychologists in the country are trained are clinical psychology and organizational psychology, the latter being an increasingly attractive field for professional development. According to Jonny Orejuela, the fact that there are many professionals with this organizational psychology profile reflects the need for in-depth study and specialization in these fields at the postgraduate level.

"The world of work remains very important; it is one of the fundamental elements that constitute identity and the human condition, and one of the benchmarks for social organization. Anyone who completes a postgraduate program of this kind will have a future because many companies increasingly need the presence of psychologists who can help develop strategies to improve not only people's performance but also their well-being at work," says the academic coordinator, who is the author of the book \* _Work Clinic: Subjective Discomfort Derived from Labor Fragmentation_ \*, published in 2018 by EAFIT Publishing.

Thus, given the growth of business activity and the expansion of the business world, graduates with a Master's degree in Work and Organizational Psychology have a great opportunity to develop their careers through this professional training, as they are experts in helping companies adapt to new working conditions and manage human processes within organizations.
